correctness.rationale: The positive Perron eigenvalue is simple; the implicit characteristic derivative is exact. When sensitive growth exceeds tolerant growth its derivative is strictly negative. Otherwise \(q=(t-\sigma)/(\nu-(t-\sigma))\) uniquely solves t-s=nu*q/(1+q)+(mu0+mc)q. At a stationary crossing \(F=q-k/[m(1+c)^2]\) has strictly positive derivative, and F>0 at large dose, proving a unique sign change when permitted. Endpoint comparison yields the exact zero-dose cutoff. The singular law follows by asymptotic inversion, and an exact rational determinant/trace verifies the two extinction roots. Standalone numerical checks corroborate but do not establish the all-parameter theorem.

value.rationale: The model addresses a nontrivial natural plasticity-versus-killing tradeoff studied in cancer mathematical biology; an exhaustive analytic classification with a rigorous unique interior optimum, an explicit critical transition, and a singular quadratic degradation of optimal suppression is useful for reasoning about model robustness. The independent rational full extinction-window example demonstrates a substantive, nonobvious failure of maximal-dose intuition. The theorem is neither a routine parameter substitution nor a finite numerical table; it gives exact all-parameter infinite statements, without claiming real-world treatment advice.
